text: Sell SGLP.L now — it's lost 99.2% from its high with the worst possible relative strength score, which means this investment is essentially destroyed and holding further just risks losing what little remains.
Sell RGTI — you're down 26%, it's 57% off its high, revenue is actually shrinking, the company is unprofitable, and there's no sign of a turnaround, so this thesis is broken.

Trim IONQ to lock in some of your 29% gain — it's unprofitable with nearly 20% short interest (meaning a lot of traders are betting against it), and quantum computing stocks remain highly speculative.
Trim LPTH to protect your 38.5% gain — a PE of 120 with negative free cash flow and four straight earnings misses means this stock is priced for perfection but delivering disappointment.
Trim LASR to bank some of your 70% profit — a tiny company trading at 113 times earnings with negative free cash flow can give back gains very quickly if sentiment shifts.
Raise your COHR stop from $295.92 to $313.89 to lock in more profit as the stock trends higher — this tightens your safety net by about 6%.

Consider adding to Microsoft while it's 21% off its high at a PE of 22 (cheap for Microsoft) with its momentum indicator turning positive — this is a rare chance to buy a best-in-class company on sale.

Consider adding to Lockheed Martin — at just 16 times earnings with steady revenue growth and a healthy 5.8% free cash flow yield (cash the business generates relative to its price), it's a reliable compounder in a strong defence spending environment.
